0NVRAOYZYUI1.event_description:
Sanhoti Durgotsav 2026 comes to Orange Coast College in Costa Mesa on 9–11 October — three days of Durga Puja in the heart of Orange County, and our largest celebration yet.

Durga Puja is the great homecoming of the Bengali year: the days when Ma Durga returns to her maternal home and an entire community organises itself around welcoming her. Sanhoti observes the full traditional sequence — Bodhon and Shashthi, Saptami, Ashtami with Pushpanjali and Sandhi Puja, Navami, and Dashami with Sindoor Khela and Bijoya greetings — with a priest conducting the rituals in full.

Around the puja runs everything that makes Durgotsav more than a religious observance. Two evenings of live concerts at the Robert B. Moore Theater on campus: Subhadeep Das Chowdhury, runner-up of Indian Idol season 14, on Friday 9 October, and Bollywood playback singer Akriti Kakar on Saturday 10 October. Cultural programs performed by Sanhoti's own children and adults. Bhog served after Pushpanjali each day, and evening food stalls with Bengali street food and sweets.

Orange Coast College sits minutes from Irvine, Newport Beach, Santa Ana and Huntington Beach, with ample parking on campus. Families travel to Sanhoti Durgotsav from across Southern California, and everyone is welcome regardless of background or faith.

39OAUSGN8P9M.event_description:
Sanhoti's Annual Picnic returned to O'Neill Regional Park in Trabuco Canyon for a full afternoon of food, games and community under the oaks.

Live kitchen. Delicious food. Fun games. An amazing afternoon — that was the promise, and the day delivered on all four.

Our live outdoor kitchen ran throughout, cooking fresh Bengali food to order rather than serving from trays. Welcome drinks of lassi and mocktails greeted arrivals, followed by a full Bengali lunch: sada bhaat, ghee and daal, with maach bhaja, alu potol chingri, shorshe ilish and methi chicken on the non-veg side, and begun bhaja, alu potol, echor'er torkari and matar paneer on the veg side. Aam'er chutney, papad bhaja, mishti doi and ice cream finished it.

On the grass there was cricket, badminton, tug of war and running races for the children. In the shade there was adda and antakshari — the real reason Bengalis picnic in the first place.

The Annual Picnic is Sanhoti's summer fixture, and the easiest event to bring a friend to. Families joined from Irvine, Tustin, Mission Viejo, Rancho Santa Margarita, Lake Forest, Aliso Viejo, Ladera Ranch and across Orange County.

UTO23AFRMNCV.event_description:
Sanhoti welcomed the Bengali New Year — Poila Boishakh — at the Norman P. Murray Community & Senior Center in Mission Viejo, Orange County.

Poila Boishakh marks the first day of the Bengali calendar and is the biggest secular celebration of the Bengali year. It belongs to everyone: no ritual requirement, no religious gatekeeping, just a shared new beginning marked with new clothes, good food and music. Traditionally families greet each other with "Shubho Nabobarsho" and businesses open their halkhata, the new ledger.

The evening ran a full Bengali New Year dinner with a choice of veg or non-veg thali. The vegetarian side brought veg momo, kaju kishmish pulao, naan, daal makhani, paneer lababdar and malpoa; the non-veg side chicken momo, chicken rezala and chingri malaikari, with the same pulao, naan and malpoa. A special mocktail was served to everyone.

Alongside the food ran a grand cultural program by kids and adults — live music including Rabindra Sangeet and adhunik, dance and recitation.

Red-and-white is customary for Poila Boishakh, and much of the hall wore it. Families joined from Mission Viejo, Irvine, Rancho Santa Margarita, Lake Forest, Aliso Viejo and across Orange County — and guests of every background were welcome.

faqs.question: Is Poila Boishakh a religious festival?
faqs.answer: No. It is a secular cultural celebration of the Bengali New Year, welcoming people of every background, faith and nationality.

SLO6F6QK8BI4.event_description:
Join us for Sanhoti's Phalaharini Kali Pujo at the Irvine Mandir, 8 Autry, Irvine, Orange County.

Rooted in Bengal's rich spiritual tradition, Phalaharini Kali Pujo is dedicated to Maa Kali. Popularised in the 19th century through Sri Ramakrishna's devotion, it is observed on the new-moon night of Jyeshtha. On this sacred day devotees pray to Maa Kali to free them from past mistakes, negativity, and to grant inner strength and peace — "phalaharini" meaning she who takes away the fruits of our actions.

It is a quieter, more inward observance than the Kali Puja of Diwali night, and for many Bengalis it is the more personal of the two. The evening includes the full puja and anjali conducted by a priest, prasad served to all who attend, and time together as a community.

Come be a part of an evening of devotion, culture and togetherness as we celebrate this beautiful legacy of Bengal. Let's gather, seek blessings, and celebrate as one family.

Open to everyone across Orange County and Southern California, whatever your background.

faqs.question: What is Phalaharini Kali Pujo?
faqs.answer: A Bengali observance dedicated to Maa Kali, held on the new-moon night of Jyeshtha. Popularised through Sri Ramakrishna's devotion, devotees pray to be freed from past mistakes and negativity and to receive inner strength and peace.

faqs.question: How is it different from Kali Puja at Diwali?
faqs.answer: Kali Puja on Diwali night is the larger, more public celebration. Phalaharini Kali Pujo falls in late spring and is a quieter, more personal observance, particularly associated with the Ramakrishna tradition.

Players of every standard turn out — from those who played competitively back home to parents returning to the game after twenty years, and teenagers growing up in Orange County who want to play with people who share their background. M261FUDR94H2.event_description:
Pithe Puli Utsab is the Bengali winter sweet festival, and Sanhoti brought it to Ladera Ranch, Orange County — the first time it has been held in the county — for an evening built entirely around the food Bengalis grow up waiting for all year.

Pithe are the rice-flour sweets made in Bengali homes around Poush Sankranti — patishapta rolled around coconut and kheer, puli boiled or fried, bhapa pithe steamed with date palm jaggery, and payesh thickened slowly with nolen gur. They take real time and real hands to make, which is exactly why they are worth gathering for.

Sanhoti families cooked and brought their own pithe to share, turning the evening into the kind of community table you cannot recreate in a restaurant. Alongside the food ran music, adda and a relaxed cultural program.

For Bengali families in Southern California, and for anyone curious about a side of Indian food that rarely appears on a menu here, Pithe Puli Utsab is one of the most distinctive evenings in the Sanhoti calendar. Love at first bite.

faqs.answer: Pithe and puli are traditional Bengali rice-flour sweets made around Poush Sankranti in winter — including patishapta, bhapa pithe and puli, usually sweetened with date palm jaggery (nolen gur).

faqs.question: Where can I find Bengali sweets in Orange County?
faqs.answer: Sanhoti serves traditional Bengali sweets at its festivals across Orange County, including the Pithe Puli Utsab in winter and payesh, rosogolla and mishti doi at Durga Puja.

WJWYE0NC4IIY.event_description:
Sanhoti celebrated Saraswati Puja 2026 at Davis Magnet School in Costa Mesa, Orange County — a spring morning devoted to the goddess of knowledge, music and the arts.

Saraswati Puja, also called Vasant Panchami, is the day Bengali families place books, instruments and pens at the feet of the goddess and ask for learning and creativity in the year ahead. The Sanhoti celebration followed the full tradition: pushpanjali offered together by everyone present, and haathe khori for our youngest children — the ceremony in which a child writes their first letters under the priest's guidance, marking the beginning of their education.

Both lunch and dinner were served, and the cultural program featured recitation, Rabindra Sangeet and dance performed by community members of every age — alongside a boshey aanko sit-and-draw session for the children and the Sanhoti General Body Meeting.

Yellow is traditionally worn on Basant Panchami, and the hall was full of it. Families joined from Costa Mesa, Irvine, Tustin, Rancho Santa Margarita and across Orange County.

faqs.question: What is haathe khori?
faqs.answer: Haathe khori is the traditional Bengali ceremony marking a child's first writing lesson, performed on Saraswati Puja day. A priest guides the child to write their first letters, symbolising the start of their education under the blessing of the goddess of learning.

faqs.question: Where does Sanhoti celebrate Saraswati Puja?
faqs.answer: Sanhoti celebrated Saraswati Puja 2026 at Davis Magnet School in Costa Mesa, Orange County, California. Venues are announced on the events page each year.

faqs.question: What should I wear to Saraswati Puja?
faqs.answer: Yellow is traditionally worn on Basant Panchami — saris, panjabis or any yellow outfit. There is no dress requirement and guests are welcome in whatever they are comfortable in.

RY3N29PQ9UJW.event_description:
Sanhoti celebrated Kali Puja 2025 at the Hindu temple on Autry in Irvine, Orange County — an evening of ritual, prasad and culture on the night Bengalis worship Goddess Kali.

Kali Puja falls on the new-moon night of Kartik, the same night as Diwali. Where much of India lights lamps for Lakshmi, Bengal turns to Ma Kali, and the puja is performed at night with its own distinct liturgy. It is one of the most atmospheric observances in the Bengali calendar.

The evening included the full puja and anjali conducted by a priest, prasad served to everyone present, and a cultural program of songs and recitation by Sanhoti members. Families joined from Irvine, Tustin, Rancho Santa Margarita, Mission Viejo and across Orange County.

Sanhoti also observes Phalaharini Kali Pujo in the spring — a second, quieter Kali observance rooted in the devotion of Sri Ramakrishna.

faqs.question: Where does Sanhoti celebrate Kali Puja in Orange County?
faqs.answer: Sanhoti has held Kali Puja at the Hindu temple at 8 Autry, Irvine, CA 92618. Check the events page for the current year.

faqs.question: How is Kali Puja different from Diwali?
faqs.answer: They fall on the same night. Diwali is the pan-Indian festival of lights; Kali Puja is the Bengali observance in which Goddess Kali is worshipped at night with a distinct liturgy.

faqs.question: Can non-Bengalis attend?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sanhoti events are open to everyone regardless of background, faith or nationality.

YHO7NY9I7CRU.event_description:
Sanhoti Durgotsav 2025 was held at Estancia High School in Costa Mesa, Orange County — three days of puja, culture, food and community that drew Bengali families from across Southern California.

The celebration followed the full traditional sequence: Shashthi and Bodhon, Saptami, Ashtami with Pushpanjali and Sandhi Puja, and Navami, closing with Dashami, Sindoor Khela and Bijoya greetings. A priest conducted the rituals in full, and the idol was the centerpiece of a pandal built by our volunteers.

Alongside the puja ran a full cultural program, including live concerts by Bengali musical duo Rathijit Bhattacharjee and Shreya M Bhattacharjee, and by playback singer Mahalakshmi Iyer, plus dance, drama and recitation performed by Sanhoti's own children and adults.

And, as every Bengali will tell you, there was the food — bhog served after Pushpanjali each day, with khichuri, labra, beguni, chatni and payesh, and evening stalls running through the cultural program.

Durga Puja 2025 laid the groundwork for our largest celebration yet: Durga Puja 2026 at Orange Coast College.

M0X449GH1WOR.event_description:
A magical evening with the melody queen. Sanhoti presented playback singer Mahalakshmi Iyer live in concert at Durga Puja 2025, at the Robert B. Moore Theater at Orange Coast College in Costa Mesa, Orange County.

Mahalakshmi Iyer is one of Indian playback singing's most versatile voices. Her breakthrough came with "Ae Ajnabee" alongside Udit Narayan for A. R. Rahman in Mani Ratnam's Dil Se, and she went on to sing for Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy and Rahman across many of the biggest films of the era — Bunty Aur Babli, Salaam Namaste, Fanaa, Dhoom 2, Ta Ra Rum Pum and Jhoom Barabar Jhoom among them. She has recorded in Hindi, Tamil, Assamese, Bengali, Telugu, Marathi, Odia, Gujarati and Kannada.

The Costa Mesa concert drew music lovers from across Southern California for an evening spanning her best-known Bollywood work and quieter, more intimate material — the range that earned her the "melody queen" description in the first place.

The concert formed part of Sanhoti Durgotsav 2025, alongside a performance by Bengali musical duo Rathijit Bhattacharjee and Shreya M Bhattacharjee.

F3PWXVMC6ML6.event_description:
Bengali musical duo Rathijit Bhattacharjee and Shreya M Bhattacharjee performed live at Sanhoti Durga Puja 2025, at the Robert B. Moore Theater at Orange Coast College in Costa Mesa, Orange County.

Rathijit Bhattacharjee is a leading figure in contemporary Bengali music — a singer, composer, lyricist and music director whose songs include "Kishori", "Radharani", "Royal Fighter", "Baba" and "Mayabi". He gave his first stage performance at the age of four, and has since scored Bengali cinema, most recently co-composing the soundtrack for the 2025 period epic Raghu Dakat. He performs alongside Shreya M Bhattacharjee.

For the Bengali community of Southern California, an evening of contemporary Bengali music performed live is a rare thing — most touring line-ups reaching the US are Bollywood-focused. This concert was programmed precisely for the audience that grew up on Bengali adhunik and wanted to hear it properly, live, in Orange County.

The performance was part of Sanhoti Durgotsav 2025, alongside a concert by playback singer Mahalakshmi Iyer.

CGEABVD2Y3BM.event_description:
Mahalaya marks the dawn of Devi Paksha — the day Goddess Durga is invoked and the countdown to Durga Puja truly begins. For Bengalis everywhere it starts before sunrise with Mahishasura Mardini, and it is one of the most emotionally charged mornings in the Bengali year.

For Mahalaya 2025, Sanhoti joined forces with Bharat Sevashram Sangha West (BSSW), Dakshini and BASC to present a combined cultural program at the Bharat Sevashram Sangha in Brea. Four organizations, one stage — Chandipath recitation, Agomoni songs, dance and choral performances by artists and community members of all ages.

Collaborations like this matter. They bring the wider Bengali community of Southern California together rather than splitting it across parallel events, and they give our children the experience of a full-scale Mahalaya morning far from Kolkata.

Mahalaya opened the season that led into Sanhoti Durga Puja 2025 in Costa Mesa.
CGEABVD2Y3BM.image_alt: Mahalaya cultural program 2025 presented by Sanhoti with BSSW, Dakshini and BASC at Bharat Sevashram Sangha, Brea, California
CGEABVD2Y3BM.meta_title: Mahalaya Cultural Program 2025 | Sanhoti, Brea CA
CGEABVD2Y3BM.meta_description: Mahalaya 2025 in Brea, California — Sanhoti with BSSW, Dakshini and BASC presenting Chandipath, Agomoni songs and dance to open Devi Paksha.

faqs.question: What is Mahalaya?
faqs.answer: Mahalaya marks the beginning of Devi Paksha and the formal invocation of Goddess Durga, seven days before Durga Puja. Bengalis traditionally listen to Mahishasura Mardini before dawn, and communities hold Chandipath recitation and Agomoni music programs.

faqs.question: Who did Sanhoti collaborate with for Mahalaya 2025?
faqs.answer: Sanhoti presented the program jointly with Bharat Sevashram Sangha West (BSSW), Dakshini and BASC, at the Bharat Sevashram Sangha in Brea, California.

faqs.question: When does Mahalaya fall?
faqs.answer: On the new moon day roughly a week before Durga Puja, usually in September or early October.

AMSNCDMJ3QRW.event_description:
Sanhoti's very first Annual Picnic brought Bengali families from across Orange County together under the oaks at O'Neill Regional Park in Trabuco Canyon. It was the day our community stopped being a mailing list and started being a neighborhood.

The day ran from breakfast to evening. Luchi, cholar dal and rabdi-jalebi opened it; lunch was a full Bengali spread of rice and ghee, macher matha diye dal, alu bhaja, mach bhaja, sorse ilish, mutton and chicken curry, with veg dal, begun bhaja, paneer masala and dhokar dalna alongside, finished with chatni, papad and sandesh. Tea, soft drinks and mocktails ran all day, and ice cream arrived in the afternoon.

Between meals there was cricket and badminton on the grass, running races and games for the children, adda under the shade for everyone who would rather talk than run, and antakshari that carried on far longer than planned.

Families joined from Irvine, Tustin, Mission Viejo, Rancho Santa Margarita, Lake Forest, Aliso Viejo and across Orange County. Guests of every background were welcome, as they are at every Sanhoti event.

faqs.answer: Yes. It is open to Bengali, Indian and non-Indian families from across Orange County and Southern California.

faqs.answer: Yes — breakfast, a full Bengali lunch, drinks throughout and an afternoon ice cream. Vegetarian options run alongside every non-veg dish.

HKSSX3WD7R0Q.event_description:
Sanhoti volunteers spent the day at Laura's House in Aliso Viejo, Orange County, supporting one of the county's most important domestic violence organizations.

Laura's House provides emergency shelter, counseling, legal advocacy and prevention education to survivors of domestic abuse across Orange County, and Sanhoti members contributed volunteer hours and donated supplies.

This was part of Sanhoti's ongoing commitment to serve the wider Orange County community, not only the Bengali families we celebrate festivals with. As a registered 501(c)(3) non-profit, Sanhoti channels a portion of every year's fundraising into local causes — hunger relief, domestic violence support, and community welfare — because being part of Southern California means showing up for the people who live here.

We are grateful to every Sanhoti member who gave their time, and to Laura's House for the work they do every single day.

ART6QV985EF3.event_description:
Srijan is Sanhoti Bengali Association's year-long workshop initiative inviting people across Orange County and Southern California to explore Indian arts — with a special focus on painting.

The program began on January 1, 2026, welcoming participants of every skill level — from first-time painters to experienced artists — to learn techniques rooted in India's visual traditions while finding their own creative voice.

Throughout the year, Sanhoti hosts guided sessions, studio meetups, and community critique circles where participants share progress, exchange ideas, and build friendships around art. Whether you grew up with rangoli and alpana at home or are discovering Indian art for the first time, Srijan is a welcoming space to create together.

The journey culminates in October 2026 with a public exhibition showcasing works from every participant — a celebration of creativity, culture, and the spirit of srijana (creation) that gives the program its name.

Srijan reflects Sanhoti's broader mission: celebrating Bengali and Indian heritage while opening our doors to everyone in the Orange County community who wants to learn, create, and connect.

artists.shortBio: Indian playback singer and composer known for Bollywood hits including "Saturday Saturday" and "Iski Uski".
artists.bio:
Akriti Kakar is an Indian playback singer and composer who has been recording professionally since 2000. She is best known for the chart-topping Bollywood tracks "Saturday Saturday" from Humpty Sharma Ki Dulhania and "Iski Uski" from 2 States.

She released her solo album, Akriti, with Sony Music India in April 2010, with compositions by Shankar Mahadevan and by Akriti herself. She has also worked extensively in television, serving as a judge on Zee Bangla's Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Li'l Champs and appearing on Colors TV's Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa.

Akriti comes from a family of playback singers — her twin sisters Sukriti and Prakriti Kakar are also established artists in the Indian music industry.

She performs at Sanhoti Durga Puja 2026 in Costa Mesa, Orange County, on Saturday 10 October 2026.

artists.shortBio: Bengali singer from Kolkata, runner-up of Indian Idol season 14 and winner of Super Singer season 4.
artists.bio:
Subhadeep Das Chowdhury is an Indian singer, composer and performer from Kolkata, West Bengal. He was the runner-up of Indian Idol season 14, and earlier won Super Singer season 4, the Bengali singing reality show. He was also among the fifteen contestants selected for Indian Idol season 11 in 2019.

Classically trained, Subhadeep taught classical music in Kolkata as a music trainer before national television brought him wider recognition. That grounding shapes his performances: a genuine classical foundation combined with fusion and contemporary versatility, and the soulful delivery he became known for on Indian Idol.

His repertoire spans Bengali and Hindi music, from Bollywood classics and high-energy anthems to quieter melodic material.

He performs at Sanhoti Durga Puja 2026 in Costa Mesa, Orange County, on Friday 9 October 2026.

artists.bio:
Mahalakshmi Iyer is an Indian playback singer, born 11 July 1976, best known for her Hindi, Assamese and Tamil recordings. She has also sung in Telugu, Marathi, Bengali, Odia, Gujarati and Kannada.

Her first released work as a playback singer was "Ae Ajnabee", sung with Udit Narayan for A. R. Rahman in Mani Ratnam's Dil Se. She went on to record extensively for Rahman and for Shankar–Ehsaan–Loy, appearing on many of the biggest Yash Raj productions of the period — Bunty Aur Babli, Salaam Namaste, Fanaa, Dhoom 2, Ta Ra Rum Pum and Jhoom Barabar Jhoom among them.

She performed at Sanhoti Durga Puja 2025 in Costa Mesa, Orange County.
